watchOS 27 will be released this fall, marking the next major update for Apple Watch. It includes a useful new feature that can extend your Apple Watch battery life: "Active Battery Extension Notifications."

watchOS 27 can actively extend your Apple Watch battery life by disabling unused features.

watchOS 27 is on the horizon, bringing two new apps, a useful new tap gesture, a brand-new default Home Screen, three health-related upgrades, and more to Apple Watch.

Another new feature in watchOS 27 is designed to extend your Apple Watch battery life.

"Active Battery Extension Notifications" are a brand-new type of prompt you may receive on your Apple Watch.

When you receive a Battery Extension prompt, it means watchOS 27 has detected that some of your features have never been used, and disabling them will help conserve battery life.

These features include various gestures, the "Raise to Speak" function that activates Siri, and the "Start Workout" reminders.

Each of these features involves background processing, which places a certain burden on battery life.

Therefore, in watchOS 27, if the system detects that you have never used these features, it will automatically disable them. The system will issue a "Battery Extension Notification" to inform you of the arrangement, and give you the option to keep them enabled.

If you frequently use these features, you will never see this prompt. Of course, you can also open "Settings" at any time to disable them yourself in exchange for longer battery life.

Apple has not specifically indicated how much additional battery life can be extended after disabling these features, but it is obvious that the energy-saving effect is worth Apple developing this brand-new battery extension feature.

Do you use your Apple Watch's "Raise to Speak," gestures, or "Start Workout" reminders? Will you continue to keep them enabled in the future? Feel free to leave a comment and share your thoughts.
